channel.title: Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly (masslawyersweekly.com)

item.title: Illinois man admits to hacking Snapchat accounts to steal nude photos
item.description: An Illinois man pleaded guilty to hacking Snapchat accounts of nearly 600 women using phishing schemes to steal and trade nude photos online.

item.title: Defense lawyer, clerk nominated as District Court judges
item.description: Gov. Maura Healey nominated a criminal defense attorney and a court clerk-magistrate as Massachusetts District Court judges.

item.title: Galvin to seek record ninth term as state secretary
item.description: Massachusetts Secretary of State William Galvin plans to seek a ninth term, citing concerns over federal election interference and census oversight.

item.title: DOJ removes Homeland Security lawyer who tells judge: ‘This job sucks’
item.description: The Department of Justice removed a DHS lawyer from a Minnesota assignment after remarks to a federal judge over immigration detention and court order compliance.

item.title: Civil rights – Excessive force
item.description: Where a plaintiff has brought claims of false arrest, malicious prosecution, excessive force, and negligence against the city of Boston and seven of its police officers, the plaintiff’s false arrest and malicious prosecution claims should be dismissed, but not his excessive force claim or his negligence claims against the city.

item.title: Patent and trademark – Preliminary injunction
item.description: Where a plaintiff alleging trade dress infringement has moved for a preliminary injunction barring the defendant from selling its allegedly infringing products while the case continues, that motion should be allowed because the plaintiff is likely to show both that that its trade dress is eligible for protection under the Lanham Act and that the defendant has infringed on it.

item.title: Employment – Whistleblower – Dodd-Frank Act
item.description: Where a plaintiff has alleged a violation of the Dodd-Frank Act, the defendant employer is entitled to summary judgment because no reasonable factfinder could find that the plaintiff has provided sufficient evidence of an adequate writing as required by the statute.

item.title: Insurance – Stay – Ripeness
item.description: Where a plaintiff insurance company has filed a complaint seeking a declaration that it has no duty to indemnify a defendant policyholder in an underlying action arising out of an altercation at a casino, the defendant’s request for a stay should be granted because the issue of indemnification is not ripe for adjudication.

item.title: Search and seizure – Custodial interrogation
item.description: Where a defendant’s motion to suppress was denied, a remand is necessary because the motion judge's factual findings were insufficient to support his conclusion that the defendant was not subjected to custodial interrogation.

item.title: Legislature creates new committee to vet initiative petitions
item.description: The Legislature on Feb. 5 agreed to appoint a 10-person joint committee to consider 11 initiative petitions that could go before voters in November.
